standard_prerequisites.name: A relatively pseudo-coherent algebra admits a resolution by a complex of finite free modules over a polynomial algebra, and a bounded above complex may be replaced by one of flat modules when testing relative pseudo-coherence
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the resolution E and the flat representative of K that the displayed computation uses.

standard_prerequisites.name: Tensoring with a bounded above complex of flat modules computes the derived tensor product, and replacing the second factor by a quasi-isomorphic complex of flat modules does not change the total complex up to quasi-isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies the chain of equalities and the quasi-isomorphism in the display that rewrites the derived base change as a total complex over R.

standard_prerequisites.name: A total complex filtered by subcomplexes whose successive quotients are m-pseudo-coherent is m-pseudo-coherent, and the cone criterion propagates relative pseudo-coherence along such filtrations
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the assertion for the total complex to the assertions for the single filtration quotients.

core_obligations: Choose a presentation A[y_1, ..., y_m] -> B, a presentation R[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A and hence a presentation of B over R, and then a resolution E of B by a complex of finite free modules over the polynomial algebra, which exists because B is pseudo-coherent relative to A (proof lines 21579-21584).

Replace K by a bounded above complex of flat A-modules and display the four-step chain of equalities and the quasi-isomorphism rewriting K tensor^L_A B as the total complex Tot(K tensor_A E) over the polynomial algebra, using that the derived tensor product may be computed by flat resolutions (proof lines 21585-21601).

Observe that the total complex carries a filtration whose successive quotients are the shifted complexes K tensor_A E^i, that all but finitely many of these vanish above degree m in cohomology and are therefore m-pseudo-coherent, and conclude by the cone criterion and induction that it suffices to handle each quotient separately (proof lines 21602-21613).

Finish by reducing to the single case of K tensor_A A[y_1, ..., y_m], which is m-pseudo-coherent relative to R by the base change lemma for relatively pseudo-coherent complexes, since E^i is finite free and vanishes for positive i (proof lines 21613-21618).
proof_roadmap: Build the presentations of B over R and the finite free resolution E of B over the polynomial algebra (proof lines 21579-21584).
Rewrite the derived base change of K along A -> B as the total complex of K tensor_A E over the polynomial algebra (proof lines 21585-21601).
Filter that total complex and use the cone criterion to reduce to the filtration quotients (proof lines 21602-21613).
Conclude with the base change lemma applied to the polynomial algebra extension, which is the remaining case (proof lines 21613-21618).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the compatibility of relative pseudo-coherence with derived base change: for finite type ring maps R -> A -> B with B pseudo-coherent relative to A, an m-pseudo-coherent (or pseudo-coherent) complex K over R stays so after the derived tensor product with B (statement lines 21567-21576). The proof rewrites the derived base change through a finite free resolution of B over a polynomial algebra, obtaining a total complex over R, and then filters that total complex by the shifted complexes K tensor_A E^i so that the cone criterion reduces the problem to a single case which is the base change along a polynomial algebra (proof lines 21578-21618). The two nontrivial moves are the rewriting of the derived base change as a total complex and the filtration argument, and both are inside the counted span. The proof refers three times to earlier lemmas of the same chapter, carried as navigation stubs.
